primary_claim: Placing sparse autoencoders only at a few residual-stream locations (rather than at every layer/component) combined with a learned binary-mask circuit-finding method (via continuous sparsification) scales SAE-based circuit discovery to Gemma 9B, finds more faithful circuits with fewer latents than existing thresholding methods like Integrated Gradients across code-output-prediction, subject-verb-agreement, and IOI tasks (one circuit achieves 95% faithfulness with <20 total latents), and the resulting minimal circuits reveal exploitable model vulnerabilities (e.g. a successful adversarial dictionary-key prompt).

effect.metric: circuit faithfulness (ratio of circuit performance to full-model performance) vs. number of latents
effect.value: learned binary masking recovers more performance with fewer latents than Integrated Gradients across all tested tasks (dictionary-key and list-index code output prediction, SVA, IOI); one circuit achieves 95% faithfulness with fewer than 20 total latents

contradicts_or_qualifies: Addresses scalability limitations of Marks et al.'s Sparse Feature Circuits approach (arXiv:2403.19647), which requires SAEs at every MLP/attention/residual layer and becomes impractical for large models
Their learned binary-masking approach outperforms thresholding-based methods like Integrated Gradients and Attribution Patching used in prior circuit-discovery work
stated_future_work: Extend the work to understand how language models perform tool use, general code interpretation, and mathematical reasoning
Analyze a broader range of code runtime prediction tasks, building on CruxEval and related benchmarks
Develop 'Layer Output Buffer SAEs' that learn an SAE on the diff between residual-stream states at two layers rather than the raw residual state
Apply the approach to find important edges within circuits, not just nodes
Extend the method to non-templatic data via a learned role-router mapping token positions to model subsets
limitations_stated: The approach doesn't find how or when something was computed, only what representations matter — a latent computed early but only needed at the end still appears in every SAE
For the IOI circuit, every name needs a latent at every single SAE to propagate through the model, making circuit analysis difficult and requiring many latents
Not yet clear what the best way is to pick the number and location of SAEs
Circuits inherit the limitations/reconstruction errors of the underlying SAEs since no error nodes are used, so faithfulness cannot exceed that of the full model with SAEs
quote: Our discovered circuits paint a clear picture of how Gemma does a given task, with one circuit achieving 95% faithfulness with <20 total latents.
